item.content: {"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=operational+distinction+between+scrambled+quantum+information+and+redundant+environmental+records&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.5771/9783748939054-585\", \"title\": [\"Article 52 Distinction between operational personal data and verification of quality of personal data Distinction between operational personal data and verification of personal data\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.5771/9783748939054-585\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.7304920\", \"title\": [\"Operational Causal Confluence: A Spacetime-Indexed Certificate for Shared Quantum Records\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Decoherence, quantum Darwinism, spectrum broadcast structure and intersubjectivity explain aspects of classical record formation, but do not specify when distinct record chains become jointly testable in spacetime. We formulate operational causal confluence (OCC) as a certificate for that task. The geometric phrase causal confluence is adopted from branching space-times, where spacelike events possess a common future witness; OCC adds quantum-record quality, provenance, persistence and nondestructive readability. A certificate belongs to a calibrated protocol, not an unrepeatable run. A token shared record is declared only when a run of a certified protocol passes a preregistered consensus rule, resolving the mismatch between ensemble probabilities and single events. A noisetolerant rule permits majority decoding without demanding unanimity as record number grows. Exact spectrum broadcast structure is sufficient once causal overlap exists; spacelike trace-preserving operations cannot alter a local certificate; and no-broadcasting confines perfectly public information to a commuting event algebra. For two records released at different times, we derive the earliest common comparison time, with t r + L/(2c) as the simultaneous special case. OCC is compatible with unitary quantum theory and neither selects outcomes nor derives the Born rule. Its value is narrower: distinguishing a stable local record from a jointly checkable record with independently characterized provenance.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7304920\", \"published\": {\"date-part…
